items.note: An entire verb phrase can be the subject of an evaluation: the action comes first, followed by its judgment or result. Learners often move the evaluation before the action or split the verb from its object; keep each action phrase intact.
Use 先 ... 再 ... to state the planned sequence of two actions; it does not say the actions have already happened. Learners often reverse the order or confuse 再 with 在.
其他 or 别的 precedes a noun to identify other members; context can make the noun understood and leave it out. Learners often put the modifier after the noun, but that order is wrong here.
Use 或 or 或者 to link alternatives in a statement; 都好 can mean either choice is fine. Learners often put 都 inside the alternatives or mistake this statement for a direct choice question.
Put the number and 口 after the eating or drinking verb and before the food or drink: 尝一口蛋糕. Here 口 counts a mouthful, not people. Learners often put the noun before the measure word.

不必 and 不用 before a verb phrase mean that an action is not necessary; 不必 is not a prohibition. Simply saying 不 + verb means not doing the action, so learners should keep 不必 or 不用 when they mean “need not.”

Use 一共 before a quantity or quantity predicate to give the total across the relevant people or amounts. Learners often use it for an individual count instead of making clear that the number is a combined total.

Use 跟 to introduce the reference item, then 一样 to say the compared items are the same in a contextually understood respect; put 不 before 一样 to express “not the same.” Learners often misplace 一样 before the reference item.
Use 又 before each of two compatible qualities to say that both apply. Learners sometimes put the second 又 after its quality; it belongs before the second quality, matching the first 又’s position.

Put 得 or 不 between the verb and its result or direction complement to say whether the result can be achieved. Use 得 for ability and 不 for inability. Learners often put the particle after the complement, but it must come before it.

items.en: I can take this bag out.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge bāo wǒ ná chū lái de
items.why: 得 must precede the complement 出来; the correct phrase is 这个包我拿得出来。

items.note: Put 下去 after a verb to show that an action continues. It describes continuing onward, not literal downward movement. Learners may mistakenly place 下去 before the verb, but the verb must come first.

Use 向 before a direction or place, followed by a movement phrase, to show where movement is headed. It does not mark the person being addressed. Learners often put the direction after the movement phrase; it belongs directly after 向.

Use 向 before a person to mark whom an introduction, request, or other interaction is directed toward. The interaction phrase follows the person. Learners often place 向 before the verb but put the person after it.

Put 更 directly before an adjective to express a greater degree relative to a stated or understood baseline. Use it when a comparison is clear from context; learners often put 更 after the adjective, where it cannot mark the degree.

When a whole proposition serves as the subject of a judgment, keep its subject and predicate together before the main predicate. Use this pattern to judge a situation or activity; learners often scramble the embedded subject and predicate or the main judgment.
Place 马上 after the subject and before the verb phrase to say that an action will happen immediately or very soon. It can also follow a time expression; learners often place it after the verb instead.

Use 如果 before the condition and 就 before the result to connect a hypothetical situation with its consequence. The result is not automatically future; learners often put 就 inside the condition or after the result verb.

Put 到 immediately after the verb to show that its goal was successfully reached or obtained. Use it for completed outcomes, not merely attempted actions. Learners often put the object before 到; keep the order verb + 到 + object, as in 拿到门票.

items.en: You got the ticket.
items.wrongPy: nǐ dào ná mén piào le
items.why: 到 must follow 拿 and precede 门票; the correct order is 你拿到门票了。

items.en: He rode to the intersection.
items.wrongPy: tā qí lù kǒu dào le
items.why: 到 must follow 骑 and precede 路口; the correct phrase is 他骑到路口了。

items.note: 得 here is the stressed modal meaning “have to,” placed after the subject and before the required action. It is not the complement marker de. Learners often move it after the verb; keep the order subject + 得 + verb phrase.

items.en: You have to bring an umbrella.
items.wrongPy: nǐ dài de sǎn
items.why: Modal 得 must precede 带, not follow it; the correct sentence is 你得带伞。

items.en: We have to set off.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men chū fā de
items.why: Modal 得 must come before 出发, not after it; the correct sentence is 我们得出发。

items.en: I have to leave right away.
items.wrongPy: wǒ de chū fā mǎ shàng
items.why: 马上 must come before 出发 within the verb phrase; the correct sentence is 我得马上出发。

items.note: 除了 introduces what is already included, and the following clause adds another fact or participant; 以外 can be omitted. Place 也 or 还 after the subject and before the predicate. Learners often put 也 before the subject.

Use 为 before the person who benefits, followed by the action: 为 + beneficiary + verb phrase. It means doing something for someone or on their behalf. Learners often put 为 after the action; keep the beneficiary immediately after 为.

Use 为 before the reason and put the emotion predicate after it: 为 + reason + emotion predicate. This pattern gives the cause of an emotion, not a person who benefits. Learners may reverse the reason and emotion; keep the reason after 为.

Use 一边 before each of two actions that happen at the same time: 一边 + action, 一边 + action. The actions should realistically overlap. Learners sometimes place the second 一边 after its action; put it before that action.

items.phrase: 他一边打网球一边说外语
items.zh: 他一边打网球，一边说外语。
items.en: He plays tennis while speaking a foreign language.
items.wrong: 他一边打网球，说外语一边。
items.wrongPy: tā yì biān dǎ wǎng qiú shuō wài yǔ yì biān
items.why: The second 一边 must come before 说外语; say 他一边打网球，一边说外语。

items.note: 把 places an identifiable object before an action that gives it a result, such as putting it away or down. The result complement follows the verb. Learners often put the complement before the verb or insert 了 between the verb and complement.

items.en: Put the plates together.
items.wrongPy: bǎ pán zi dào fàng yí kuàir
items.why: 到一块儿 follows 放 to give its result; the correct order is 把盘子放到一块儿。

items.note: Use 先 before the first action and 然后 before the next action to mark chronological order. The pattern can describe planned or completed actions. Learners may put 然后 before the first action; keep the sequence markers in the order 先, 然后.

Put 总 or 总是 immediately after the subject and before the predicate to describe a habit or an invariably repeated event; complaints may exaggerate. Learners often put it after the verb, but it normally precedes the whole predicate.
Place 刚 or 刚刚 before the verb phrase to say an event happened very recently relative to a reference time. Learners often put it after the verb or split the verb phrase; keep it before the action.

Put 到处 before the verb phrase when an action happens across many locations, rather than moving toward one destination. Learners often put it after the verb, but it functions here as an adverbial before the action.
After an activity verb, 起来 can mark that the activity begins; with 跳, it can also mean jump upward. Learners must keep 起来 after the verb, not place it before the action.

items.en: The story started being told.
items.wrongPy: gù shi qǐ lai jiǎng le
items.why: 起来 must follow the activity verb 讲; the correct order is 故事讲起来了。

items.note: Put the number between the verb and 遍 to count complete repetitions from start to finish. Learners may reverse 一 and 遍 or confuse 遍 with a single event rather than one full pass.
“的话” marks the condition and follows it; “就” then introduces the result. It means “if,” not literal speech. Learners often put “的话” in the result clause or reverse the result’s verb-object order.

应该 goes after the subject and before a verb phrase to express advice or a reasonable expectation, not a guaranteed outcome. Learners may put it after the action or separate it from the subject; keep the order subject + 应该 + action.

items.en: Adults should take care of patients.
items.wrongPy: dà ren bìng rén yīng gāi zhào gù
items.why: 应该 should follow the subject 大人 and precede the action 照顾病人.

items.note: Use “才” before a quantity to indicate an amount smaller than expected. It can describe an amount, price, or limited number of things. Learners often omit the required measure word or put the quantity before “才.”

Put “才” after the focused subject and before the predicate to emphatically reject a competing judgment; “呢” may add emphasis. Learners often move “才” after the predicate or put “不” in the wrong position.

Place 越来越 immediately before an adjective to describe a degree that keeps increasing over time, without naming a comparison target. Learners often put the adjective first or treat 越来越 as a time phrase after it.
Use 被 to present the affected subject as undergoing an event; an agent may follow 被. The verb needs an event-completion marker here, and learners often omit or misplace 了.
Use 把 when the object is identifiable and the sentence states where it ends up: 把 + object + verb + 在/到 + place. Learners often put the verb before the object or omit the resulting location.
In this result complement, 走 follows a verb to show that something is taken away or departs. It marks the outcome, not simply walking; learners often mistake it for a standalone motion verb.

items.en: He took the mineral water away.
items.wrongPy: tā bǎ dài zǒu kuàng quán shuǐ le
items.why: 走 must follow 带 in 带走; placing it before the object breaks the result-complement order.

items.note: Put 一会儿 before the verb phrase to say an event will happen shortly. Use it for near-future timing, not for how long an action lasts; after the verb, it usually indicates duration.

items.en: I’ll answer in a moment.
items.wrongPy: wǒ yí huìr le jiē
items.why: 了 cannot appear before the verb here; the correct sentence is 我一会儿接。

items.en: The mail will arrive shortly.
items.wrongPy: yóu jiàn yí huìr le dào
items.why: 了 cannot appear before the verb here; the correct sentence is 邮件一会儿到。

items.note: 还 before an adjective phrase can mean “fairly” or “acceptably,” while context may also give it a “still” sense. Learners often assume every 还 means “still” or “also”; 很 may follow 还.

items.en: The shirt fits okay.
items.wrongPy: chèn shān hé shì hái
items.why: 还 should precede the adjective 合适, as in 衬衫还合适.

items.en: The top fits okay.
items.wrongPy: shàng yī hé shì hái
items.why: 还 belongs before 合适 here, not after it.

items.en: This top is fairly suitable.
items.wrongPy: zhè jiàn shàng yī hěn hái hé shì
items.why: 很 cannot precede 还 in this pattern; the correct order is 还合适.

items.note: 愿意 comes before a verb phrase to express willingness or readiness, not a future event. Learners often treat it like a future marker or insert aspect particles between 愿意 and its verb.
This pattern means not even one: put 一 plus a measure word and noun before 也/都, then 不/没 before the verb. Learners often move 也/都 or choose negation without regard to event aspect.

Place 好像 before the predicate to mark an impression rather than confirmed knowledge. It can precede an adjective phrase or a verb phrase; learners often put 很 after the adjective instead of before it.
越...越... links two changing degrees: as the first predicate increases, the second does too. Put 越 immediately before each predicate; learners often omit or strand the second 越.
只要 introduces a sufficient condition, and 就 introduces its result. Use the pair across the condition and result clauses; learners often attach 就 to the condition or leave it at the sentence end.

几乎 comes before the predicate to show that a state or limit is nearly reached. Keep the predicate’s original positive or negative polarity. Learners often move 几乎 after the predicate or place 都 after the negative ending.

子 is a neutral-tone suffix in established nouns such as 屋子 and 箱子; it does not automatically make a noun diminutive. Keep it attached to the noun stem. Learners may wrongly separate 子 or treat it as a freely added smallness marker.

items.en: The box is very big.
items.wrongPy: xiāng zi dà hěn
items.why: 很 belongs before 大 in this predicate; it cannot be placed after the adjective.

items.note: 为了 introduces an intended goal, followed by the action taken for that purpose; it does not claim the goal was achieved. Keep the goal before the action clause. Learners sometimes scramble the verb, adverb, and object in the action clause.

必须 comes before a verb phrase to express that an action is required. To say an action is unnecessary, Mandarin uses dedicated forms meaning “need not,” rather than simply placing a negator before 必须. Learners often misuse that simple negation or move the subject after 必须.

又 before a verb phrase presents an action or event as recurring or already realized; 再 is generally used for a further action that is still in the future. Learners often put 又 after the verb or its ending 了.

items.en: The train is late again.
items.wrongPy: huǒ chē wǎn diǎn yòu le
items.why: 又 must precede 晚点, with 了 after the verb phrase; the correct order is 火车又晚点了。

items.en: It seems the principal is having another meeting.
items.wrongPy: kàn lái xiào zhǎng kāi huì yòu le
items.why: 又 must precede 开会, with 了 after the verb phrase; the correct order is 看来，校长又开会了。

items.note: Put 比 between the compared item and the reference, then place 更 or 还 before the adjective to emphasize a greater degree. Use this when the comparison is especially strong. Learners often put 还 before the reference, where it does not fit this pattern.

关于 introduces the topic that the following statement will discuss. Use it to frame a comment about something, rather than to name the target of an attitude. Learners can mistakenly treat it as though it means “toward” or “concerning” in every context.

不但 introduces the first point, and 而且 introduces an added, often stronger point. Use the pattern to emphasize that both points apply. Learners may jumble the two connectors or leave 而且 without the second clause.

items.phrase: 电子书不但有用而且常见
items.zh: 电子书不但有用，而且常见。
items.en: E-books are not only useful but also common.
items.wrong: 电子书不但而且有用常见。
items.wrongPy: diàn zǐ shū bú dàn ér qiě yǒu yòng cháng jiàn
items.why: 不但 must introduce the first point before 而且; put 有用 before 而且, as in the original.

items.phrase: 电子书不但常见而且有用
items.zh: 电子书不但常见，而且有用。
items.en: E-books are not only common, but also useful.
items.wrong: 电子书不但而且常见有用。
items.wrongPy: diàn zǐ shū bú dàn ér qiě cháng jiàn yǒu yòng
items.why: 不但 must introduce the first point before 而且; put 常见 before 而且, as in the original.

items.note: 看来 introduces a conclusion drawn from indications, so the statement is presented as apparent rather than certain. Put it before the inference. Learners can mistake it for a marker of established fact instead of a cautious judgment.

items.en: It seems the principal is having another meeting.
items.wrongPy: kàn lái xiào zhǎng yòu le kāi huì
items.why: 了 follows the verb 开会 to mark the event; the original puts it after 开会.

items.note: Attach 员 to a role or organization stem only in established compounds, such as 服务员 and 检票员. It names a person in that role; learners often assume any noun can take 员 or move 员 away from its stem.

items.en: The athlete exercises on the sports field.
items.wrongPy: yùn dòng yuán qiú chǎng zài duàn liàn
items.why: 在 must precede 球场; the correct sentence is 运动员在球场锻炼。

items.note: Put 除了 before the excluded person or group, optionally add 以外, then use 都 with the remaining group’s predicate. It means everyone or everything in the stated group except the exception does the predicate; learners often omit 都 or include the exception in the group.

Use 班 as the measure word for a scheduled departure or service, followed by the service noun, as in 班高铁. Do not treat 班 here as a class-group noun or insert another measure word between 班 and the noun.

items.en: There are still two high-speed train services.
items.wrongPy: hái yǒu liǎng bān gè gāo tiě
items.why: 个 cannot follow 班 here; the correct measure phrase is 两班高铁。

items.en: There is one more high-speed train.
items.wrongPy: hái yǒu yì bān gè gāo tiě
items.why: 个 cannot follow 班 here; the correct measure phrase is 一班高铁。

items.note: 只有 introduces a necessary condition, and 才 introduces its result; the pattern says the result is possible only under that condition, not that the condition guarantees it. Learners often omit 才 or place it before the wrong clause.

items.en: Only by taking part in the competition can you score points.
items.wrongPy: zhǐ yǒu cān jiā bǐ sài dé fēn cái
items.why: 才 must precede the result predicate, not follow it; the correct sentence is 只有参加比赛，才得分。

items.phrase: 只有认真练习水平才提高
items.zh: 只有认真练习，水平才提高。
items.en: Only by practicing carefully can your skill improve.
items.wrong: 只有认真练习，才水平提高。
items.wrongPy: zhǐ yǒu rèn zhēn liàn xí cái shuǐ píng tí gāo
items.why: 才 must precede the result predicate, not its subject; the correct sentence is 只有认真练习，水平才提高。

items.note: Put a question word such as 什么 before 都 and then give the predicate; the phrase means every possible thing, not a question. Learners often put 都 after the predicate, but it belongs directly after the question word here.

差不多 comes before a quantity to mean approximately that amount; 不 is part of this fixed expression, not a separate negation. Learners may omit the measure word 个, but it is needed between 十 and 游客 here.

大概 before a predicate marks an inference that something is probable, not confirmed. Learners may move it after the predicate, but it belongs before the part being presented as probable; with 有, it also comes before the quantity.

比较 comes immediately before an adjective to mean relatively or fairly, without naming an object of comparison. Learners sometimes place 比较 after the adjective, but that reverses the required order for this meaning.

items.en: This competition is fairly famous.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge bǐ sài yǒu míng bǐ jiào
items.why: 比较 must come before 有名; the correct phrase is 这个比赛比较有名。

items.note: Use this conjunction between two clauses when the second contrasts with the first. Here it means “but,” not “can.” Learners may confuse it with a possibility word or put the negative after the verb instead of before it.

Place this expression before a complete statement to present it as expected or unsurprising. It introduces the whole statement, rather than modifying just the verb. Learners may put the subject after the modal verb or scramble a noun phrase.

在...中 frames an activity or context, with 在 before the process and 中 after it; the statement follows. Learners often place 在 after 中 or put 中 before the process; keep the two markers around the process.

items.en: Points matter in a competition.
items.wrongPy: bǐ sài zhōng zài fēn hěn zhòng yào
items.why: 在 must precede the process, not follow 中; a correct frame is 在比赛中。

items.en: He scored in the competition.
items.wrongPy: tā zài zhōng bǐ sài dé fēn le
items.why: 中 must follow 比赛, not precede it; the correct order is 他在比赛中得分了。

items.phrase: 在会议中咱们解决难题
items.zh: 在会议中，咱们解决难题。
items.en: During the meeting, let's solve the difficult problem.
items.wrong: 在中会议，咱们解决难题。
items.wrongPy: zài zhōng huì yì zán men jiě jué nán tí
items.why: 中 must follow 会议, not precede it; the correct order is 在会议中，咱们解决难题。

items.note: The pattern number + 所 + institution noun uses 所 as a measure word for institutions such as schools. Use it when counting those institutions, not buildings in general. No example phrases were provided, so there are no near-miss items.

Put “该” after the subject and before the action or description that is advisable or due. It expresses what someone ought to do, not necessarily a scheduled turn. Learners often place “该” after the verb phrase.

items.en: This time, it’s my turn to check.
items.wrongPy: zhè huí wǒ chá gāi
items.why: “该” must precede the action; the correct order is “这回该我查”.

items.note: Put 终于 before the verb phrase to show that an event happened after delay or difficulty. Learners often insert it inside a verb-object unit or put it after the verb; keep it before the complete predicate.

items.en: She finally stopped moving.
items.wrongPy: tā zhàn zhōng yú zhù le
items.why: 终于 cannot split 站住; the correct order is 她终于站住了。

items.note: 下 follows the verb as a result complement when it means retain, accept, record, or set down. In 把 sentences, the object may come before the verb-complement; learners often move 下 before the verb.

items.en: I'll note down this point.
items.wrongPy: wǒ jì zhè ge diǎn xià
items.why: 下 follows 记 before the object, as in 我记下这个点。

items.note: Use this frame to state an impression explicitly: put the person or thing first, then the appearance verb, then an adjective phrase. It reports how something seems, not a literal act of looking upward. Learners often put the adjective before the appearance verb.

items.en: The customer looks quite worried.
items.wrongPy: kè rén kàn qǐ lai tǐng de jí
items.why: The particle does not go between the degree word and adjective; place it after the adjective phrase.

items.en: This approach looks no good.
items.wrong: 这个办法看起来不行很。
items.wrongPy: zhè ge bàn fǎ kàn qǐ lai bù xíng hěn
items.why: The degree word cannot follow this adjective phrase; say the approach looks no good.

items.note: 挺 + adjective + 的 is a colloquial way to say something is quite or rather a certain way, often in an evaluation. Final 的 commonly completes the pattern. Learners may put 的 before the adjective; it belongs after the adjective here.

items.en: The customer looks quite worried.
items.wrongPy: kè rén tǐng kàn qǐ lai jí de
items.why: 挺 cannot modify 看起来 in this position; say 客人看起来挺急的。

items.note: Place 坏了 after a predicate that can express an intense state, such as 急 or 着急, to mean “terribly.” Learners may treat 坏 as a free intensifier and put it before the state; it belongs after the whole predicate.

items.en: I’m terribly worried.
items.wrongPy: wǒ huài jí le
items.why: 坏了 must follow the whole state predicate; the correct order is 我急坏了。

items.en: She got terribly worried.
items.wrongPy: tā huài zháo jí le
items.why: 坏了 follows the complete predicate 着急; the correct order is 她着急坏了。

items.note: Topic + 不怎么样 gives an unimpressed evaluation, meaning that something is not particularly good. It is a statement pattern, not a question asking how something is. Learners should keep 不怎么样 together after the topic rather than moving 不 to another position.

items.en: The exercise is not so great.
items.wrongPy: bù zěn me yàng liàn xí
items.why: 不怎么样 follows the topic in this statement; say 练习不怎么样。

items.en: The competition was not particularly good.
items.wrongPy: bǐ sài zěn me yàng bù
items.why: 不 cannot be placed after 怎么样 here; say 比赛不怎么样。

items.en: The sports meet was not particularly good.
items.wrongPy: yùn dòng huì bù de zěn me yàng
items.why: 的 cannot go between 不 and 怎么样; say 运动会不怎么样。

items.note: 一般来说 introduces a generalization, usually at the start of a sentence, and signals that exceptions may exist. It is followed by a statement. Learners should not treat it as part of the subject or rearrange the words of the statement after it.

items.phrase: 一般来说练习比较简单
items.zh: 一般来说，练习比较简单。
items.en: Generally speaking, the exercise is fairly simple.
items.wrong: 一般来说，练习简单比较。
items.wrongPy: yì bān lái shuō liàn xí jiǎn dān bǐ jiào
items.why: 比较 should precede 简单; say 一般来说，练习比较简单。

items.note: 住 follows a compatible verb to mark a secured or maintained result, with 了 after 住 when the result is completed. Learners often put 了 between the verb and 住, breaking the verb-complement unit.

items.en: She stopped moving.
items.wrongPy: tā zhàn le zhù le
items.why: 了 cannot split the verb from its result complement; say 她站住了。

items.en: I caught it.
items.wrongPy: wǒ jiē le zhù
items.why: 住 must directly follow 接 before 了; the correct phrase is 我接住了。

items.en: She finally stopped moving.
items.wrongPy: tā zhōng yú zhàn le zhù le
items.why: Keep 住 next to 站, with 了 after the complement; say 她终于站住了。

items.note: 家 forms established occupation or expertise nouns such as 画家. It is not a suffix learners can freely move or attach anywhere; keep it after the field stem, and place 也 before the verb it modifies.

items.en: He is a painter.
items.wrongPy: tā shì jiā huà
items.why: 家 follows the field stem to form 画家; say 他是画家。

items.en: Artists also pay attention to the world.
items.wrongPy: huà jiā guān zhù yě shì jiè
items.why: 也 cannot split 关注 from its object here; it belongs before 关注, as in 画家也关注世界。

items.note: Place 极了 after a gradable description to express an extreme degree; the final 了 is part of this degree expression, not past tense. Learners sometimes move 极了 before the description.

items.en: That sounds extremely unpleasant!
items.wrongPy: jí le nán tīng
items.why: 极了 follows the description, rather than preceding it; the correct phrase is 难听极了！

items.en: The top is extremely ugly.
items.wrongPy: shàng yī jí le nán kàn
items.why: 极了 must follow 难看; the correct sentence is 上衣难看极了。

items.en: This sound is extremely unpleasant.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge shēng yīn jí le nán tīng
items.why: 极了 must follow 难听, not precede it; the correct sentence is 这个声音难听极了。

items.note: 对我来说 sets the perspective for the judgment that follows, roughly “for me.” Keep the reference noun phrase between 对 and 来说; learners may wrongly reverse 我 and 来说 or confuse the scope phrase with the judgment.

Place 从 before a starting time and 起 immediately after it to mark the boundary from which the statement applies. Learners often move 起 to the end or treat it as a free particle; keep it attached to the time phrase.

items.en: Starting the year after next, I'll exercise too.
items.wrongPy: cóng qǐ hòu nián wǒ yě duàn liàn
items.why: 起 must follow the starting time, so say 从后年起，我也锻炼。

items.en: Starting in autumn, I also climb mountains.
items.wrongPy: cóng qǐ qiū tiān wǒ yě pá shān
items.why: 起 must follow the starting time, so say 从秋天起，我也爬山。

items.en: Starting in autumn, I work from home.
items.wrongPy: cóng qiū tiān wǒ qǐ zài jiā gōng zuò
items.why: 起 belongs after the starting time, so say 从秋天起，我在家工作。

items.note: 需要 can take an action, meaning someone needs to do it, or a noun, meaning someone needs that thing. Keep the needed action or thing after 需要; learners often put it before 需要 as if English word order applied.

items.en: I need takeout.
items.wrongPy: wǒ wài mài xū yào
items.why: The thing needed follows 需要; say 我需要外卖。

items.en: Do we need takeout?
items.wrongPy: wǒ men wài mài xū yào ma
items.why: The thing needed follows 需要; say 我们需要外卖吗？

items.en: Does this room need air conditioning?
items.wrongPy: zhè ge wū zi kōng tiáo xū yào ma
items.why: The thing needed follows 需要; say 这个屋子需要空调吗？

items.note: Some verbs combine with 起 to mean recalling or bringing something to mind, and the object follows the whole verb-complement unit. Learners often put 起 after the object; learn compatible combinations such as 记起 and 想起.

items.en: I remembered the sound.
items.wrongPy: wǒ jì shēng yīn qǐ le
items.why: 起 must follow 记 and precede the object, so say 我记起声音了。

items.en: I remembered that sound.
items.wrongPy: wǒ jì nà shēng yīn qǐ le
items.why: 起 must follow 记 and precede the object, so say 我记起那声音了。

items.note: 上 follows a compatible verb to mark attachment, contact, or closure, with the object in the position required by the construction. Learners often move 上 before the verb; keep combinations such as 接上, 挂上, and 关上 intact.

items.en: It's connected now.
items.wrongPy: shàng jiē le
items.why: 上 must follow 接, so say 接上了。

items.note: With compatible activity verbs, 上 follows the verb to show that an activity has begun or someone has become engaged in it. Learners often put 上 before the verb; keep the sequence verb plus 上, as in 聊上.

items.en: They started chatting.
items.wrongPy: tā men shàng liáo le
items.why: 上 must follow 聊, so say 他们聊上了。

items.en: My uncle and I started chatting.
items.wrongPy: shū shu hé wǒ shàng liáo le
items.why: 上 must follow 聊, so say 叔叔和我聊上了。

items.en: The guest and my uncle started chatting.
items.wrongPy: kè rén hé shū shu liáo le shàng
items.why: 上 must follow 聊 and precede 了, so say 客人和叔叔聊上了。

items.note: Put this certainty word after the subject and before the predicate to say that a proposition is definitely true or expected. It expresses confidence, not proof. Learners often put it after the verb or place it after a modal verb.

items.en: You can definitely do it.
items.wrongPy: nǐ xíng yí dìng
items.why: The certainty word comes before the predicate; say that you can definitely do it.

items.en: I believe he can do it for sure.
items.wrongPy: wǒ xìn yí dìng tā xíng
items.why: The certainty word belongs before the embedded predicate, after its subject; say you believe he can do it for sure.

items.note: Use 在 + domain + 上 to limit a statement to a particular respect, rather than to describe a physical surface. Learners may omit 上 after the domain; in this pattern it marks the scope of the claim.

items.en: There are changes in life.
items.wrongPy: zài shēng huó yǒu biàn huà
items.why: The scope marker is missing after the domain; it belongs after 生活.

items.en: He is quite satisfied with his health.
items.wrongPy: zài jiàn kāng shàng tā mǎn yì hěn
items.why: The degree word must precede the adjective; 很 belongs before 满意.

items.phrase: 在生活上他们都有变化
items.zh: 在生活上，他们都有变化。
items.en: Their lives have all changed.
items.wrong: 在生活上，他们有都变化。
items.wrongPy: zài shēng huó shàng tā men yǒu dōu biàn huà
items.why: 都 must precede the verb; it belongs before 有, not after it.

items.note: Put 一直 before the predicate to say that a state or activity continues throughout an interval. It can precede a verb phrase or a state such as 很安静. Learners often move it after the predicate, where it becomes a dangling, incomplete element.

items.en: He stays at the gym the whole time.
items.wrongPy: tā yì zhí bīn guǎn zài tǐ yù guǎn
items.why: The location phrase must be 在体育馆; putting 宾馆 before 在 also introduces a word not in this phrase.

items.note: Attach 下来 directly after a verb to show that an activity persisted through an interval up to a reference point. Here it does not mean physical downward movement. Learners sometimes reverse its components; the order must be verb + 下来.

items.en: He kept going.
items.wrongPy: tā jiān chí lái xià
items.why: 下来 must follow the verb in that order; the original has 坚持下来.

items.en: It isn't easy to keep going.
items.wrongPy: jiān chí lái xià bù róng yì
items.why: 下来 must follow the verb in that order; the original has 坚持下来.

items.en: With continued practice, one’s skill improved.
items.wrongPy: liàn xí xià shuǐ píng tí gāo le lái
items.why: 下来 must stay together after the verb; the original has 练习下来.

items.en: This habit has continued.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge xí guàn jiān chí xià le lái
items.why: 下来 must stay together after the verb; the original has 坚持下来.

items.note: Use 在 + condition + 下 before a statement to describe circumstances or influence, not a physical position below something. Learners may put 下 in the wrong place; it closes the condition phrase after its noun phrase.

items.phrase: 在他的影响下生活变了
items.zh: 在他的影响下，生活变了。
items.en: Under his influence, life changed.
items.wrong: 在影响他的下，生活变了。
items.wrongPy: zài yǐng xiǎng tā de xià shēng huó biàn le
items.why: 下 must close the condition phrase after 影响; the original places it there.

items.phrase: 在坏习惯的影响下生活变了
items.zh: 在坏习惯的影响下，生活变了。
items.en: Under the influence of bad habits, life changed.
items.wrong: 在坏习惯影响的下，生活变了。
items.wrongPy: zài huài xí guàn yǐng xiǎng de xià shēng huó biàn le
items.why: 的 must connect 坏习惯 to 影响, and 下 follows the whole condition phrase.

items.phrase: 在坏习惯的影响下他也胖了
items.zh: 在坏习惯的影响下，他也胖了。
items.en: Under the influence of bad habits, he also gained weight.
items.wrong: 在坏习惯的影响下，也他胖了。
items.wrongPy: zài huài xí guàn de yǐng xiǎng xià yě tā pàng le
items.why: 也 must precede the predicate subject phrase here; it belongs after 他.

items.phrase: 在他的影响下他的习惯变了
items.zh: 在他的影响下，他的习惯变了。
items.en: Under his influence, his habits changed.
items.wrong: 在他的下影响，他的习惯变了。
items.wrongPy: zài tā de xià yǐng xiǎng tā de xí guàn biàn le
items.why: 下 must follow the full condition phrase, not split 他的影响.

items.note: 一点儿也不 goes before an adjective or attitude predicate to negate it completely, meaning “not at all.” Learners often put 不 before 一点儿; keep the order 一点儿也不.

items.en: I don't trust him at all.
items.wrongPy: wǒ bù yì diǎnr yě xìn tā
items.why: 不 must follow 一点儿也; the correct order is 我一点儿也不信他。

items.phrase: 这个屋子一点儿也不旧
items.zh: 这个屋子一点儿也不旧。
items.en: This room isn’t old at all.
items.wrong: 这个屋子不一点儿也旧。
items.wrongPy: zhè ge wū zi bù yì diǎnr yě jiù
items.why: 不 must follow 一点儿也; the correct order is 这个屋子一点儿也不旧。

items.note: 一定 comes before a verb phrase to make an insistent instruction or express resolve, as in “be sure to do something.” Learners may place 一定 after the verb; keep it before the whole action.
Repeat 一会儿 before each action or state to describe alternating actions or changing states over short intervals. Learners may scramble a verb and its object; keep each verb before its object.

items.phrase: 他一会儿着急一会儿放心
items.zh: 他一会儿着急，一会儿放心。
items.en: One moment he is anxious, the next he is reassured.
items.wrong: 一会儿着急他，一会儿放心。
items.wrongPy: yí huìr zháo jí tā yí huìr fàng xīn
items.why: 他 cannot follow 着急 in this pattern; the correct order is 他一会儿着急，一会儿放心。

items.phrase: 一会儿收邮件一会儿发邮件
items.zh: 一会儿收邮件，一会儿发邮件。
items.en: One moment I collect mail, the next I send mail.
items.wrong: 一会儿收邮件，一会儿邮件发。
items.wrongPy: yí huìr shōu yóu jiàn yí huìr yóu jiàn fā
items.why: 邮件 must follow 发; the correct phrase is 一会儿收邮件，一会儿发邮件。

items.note: 老 + surname is a familiar way to address or refer to someone, as in 老王. Use it when the relationship and context make this form appropriate; it does not simply mean the person is old. Keep 老 immediately before the surname, not after the predicate.

items.en: My uncle, Wang, is very healthy.
items.wrongPy: wǒ shū shu hěn jiàn kāng lǎo wáng
items.why: 老王 must stay together as the familiar surname address before the predicate; the sentence leaves it dangling at the end.

items.note: 只 goes before a verb phrase to restrict the action or its object, meaning “only.” Learners may put 只 after the verb; place it before the verb phrase, as in 只需要.

items.en: He only needs a mailbox.
items.wrongPy: tā xū yào yóu xiāng zhī
items.why: 只 cannot go after the object here; it must precede 需要, as in 他只需要邮箱。

items.en: He only needs a box.
items.wrongPy: tā xū yào xiāng zi zhī
items.why: 只 cannot go after the object here; it must precede 需要, as in 他只需要箱子。

items.note: Use 只是 after the subject and before the predicate to limit the statement to “just” or “only” that predicate. It does not introduce a contrast like “but.” A common mistake is putting it after the predicate or treating it as a contrast marker.

items.en: This is only a photo.
items.wrongPy: zhè zhǐ shì de zhào piàn
items.why: The extra 的 leaves an incomplete modifier; the correct sentence ends with 照片.

items.note: A direction such as 北方 can serve as the subject or location for a predicate, including 有 to say something exists there. It names a region, not necessarily a political or cultural group. Do not insert 在 before 有 in this pattern.

items.en: There are sheep in the north.
items.wrongPy: běi fāng zài yǒu yáng
items.why: 在 cannot be inserted before 有 here; the correct sentence is 北方有羊。

items.note: Put a place noun before 东、南、西、 or 北 to indicate a cardinal direction relative to that place. This point has no example phrases, so no near-miss items are provided. Do not confuse this pattern with a direction word used alone as a region.

Put 中间 after the noun phrase naming the reference area or objects to locate something in the middle or between them. The reference comes first; learners may mistakenly attach 的 after 中间 and leave the sentence unfinished.

items.en: The box is in the middle of the room.
items.wrongPy: xiāng zi zài wū zi zhōng jiān de
items.why: The final 的 leaves the location phrase unfinished; the correct sentence ends with 中间。

items.note: Put 怎样 before the verb phrase to ask how an action is performed. It asks about the manner of the action, not the identity of its object. Learners often move 怎样 before the subject or place it after the verb.

items.en: How do you take photos?
items.wrongPy: zěn yàng nǐ pāi zhào
items.why: 怎样 must precede the verb phrase, not the subject; say 你怎样拍照？

items.en: How do you choose a box?
items.wrongPy: zěn yàng nǐ xuǎn zé xiāng zi
items.why: 怎样 belongs before 选择箱子, not before 你; say 你怎样选择箱子？

items.note: Repeat the same question word in two clauses to link matching choices, with each question word in its normal role in its clause. Learners sometimes move the question word out of its role or change the clause order.

items.en: I’ll choose whatever you choose.
items.wrongPy: nǐ shén me xuǎn wǒ xuǎn shén me
items.why: 什么 is the object of 选 and must follow it; say 你选什么，我选什么。

items.phrase: 你怎样选择我怎样选择
items.zh: 你怎样选择，我怎样选择。
items.en: I choose however you choose.
items.wrong: 怎样你选择，我怎样选择。
items.wrongPy: zěn yàng nǐ xuǎn zé wǒ zěn yàng xuǎn zé
items.why: 怎样 must precede the verb phrase, not the subject; say 你怎样选择，我怎样选择。

items.note: Repeat a measure word, then use 都 before the predicate to emphasize every individual member. This pattern applies to groups. Learners often put 都 after the predicate, where it cannot mark the whole group correctly.

items.en: Every one is healthy.
items.wrongPy: gè gè jiàn kāng dōu
items.why: 都 must come before the predicate, not after it; say 个个都健康。

items.en: Every guest is in a hurry.
items.wrongPy: kè rén gè gè zháo jí dōu
items.why: 都 must precede 着急; placing it after the predicate is wrong.

items.note: Repeat the same number and measure word to describe successive groups or actions, often one by one. 地 may be omitted, but if used it follows the full repeated phrase. Learners sometimes place 地 between its two halves.

items.en: Collect the letters one by one.
items.wrongPy: yì fēng de yì fēng shōu xìn
items.why: 地 must follow the complete repeated phrase, not split it; say 一封一封地收信。

items.en: Check the boxes one by one.
items.wrongPy: yí gè yí gè jiǎn chá de xiāng zi
items.why: 地 must follow the repeated phrase and precede the verb; say 一个一个地检查箱子。

items.note: Use a number plus 碗 or 盘 before the food noun to count bowlfuls or platefuls, rather than naming the container as an object. Learners often put the measure before the number.

items.en: A plate of bananas.
items.wrongPy: pán yì xiāng jiāo
items.why: The number must precede the measure and food noun; the correct order is 一盘香蕉.

items.note: After a suitable negative or modal, 什么 can mean “anything” or “any”; it follows the verb. Learners often move 什么 before the verb, or assume every modal licenses this reading.

items.en: He doesn’t need anything.
items.wrongPy: tā bù shén me xū yào
items.why: 不 must precede 需要, while 什么 follows it; the correct order is 他不需要什么.

items.en: The guest doesn’t need any boxes.
items.wrongPy: kè rén bù shén me xū yào xiāng zi
items.why: 什么 follows 需要 in this pattern; the correct order is 客人不需要什么箱子.

items.note: 特别 before an adjective marks an especially high degree. Use it to intensify a quality; learners may mistake it for an adjective meaning “unusual” or put it after the adjective.

items.en: He is especially worried.
items.wrongPy: tā zháo jí tè bié
items.why: 特别 must come before the adjective it intensifies; the correct order is 他特别着急.

items.en: This room is especially old.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge wū zi jiù tè bié
items.why: 特别 must come before the adjective it intensifies; the correct order is 这个屋子特别旧.

items.note: 就 comes before the noun phrase whose scope it restricts; here it singles out this mailbox as the one that has mail. Learners often place 就 after the noun phrase.

items.en: Only this mailbox has mail.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge jiù yóu xiāng yǒu xìn
items.why: 就 must precede the restricted noun phrase 这个邮箱; the correct order is 就这个邮箱有信.

items.note: 其实 comes before the statement and signals that you are correcting or qualifying what someone might expect. Learners may place it inside the statement or confuse 有些 here with “some”; it means “somewhat” before 着急.

items.en: Actually, I’m somewhat worried.
items.wrongPy: qí shí wǒ zháo jí yǒu xiē
items.why: 有些 must come before the adjective, not after it; keep the original order.

items.en: Actually, uncle is at the gym.
items.wrongPy: qí shí shū shu tǐ yù guǎn zài
items.why: 在 must come before the location; the original phrase has the correct order.

items.note: 差不多 before 了 says that the work is nearly complete, without claiming it is fully done. Keep 工作 as the subject before this completion phrase; learners may mistake 差不多 for a duration expression.

items.en: The work is nearly done.
items.wrongPy: le gōng zuò chà bu duō
items.why: The subject must come before the near-completion phrase; use the original order.

items.en: Only at the end did I receive the letter.
items.wrongPy: zuì hòu cái xìn shōu dào
items.why: 收到 must precede its object; the original phrase has the correct verb-object order.

items.en: He only understood in the end.
items.wrongPy: tā míng bai zuì hòu cái
items.why: 才 belongs before the verb phrase here, not at the end; keep the original order.

items.note: 有些 before an adjective means “somewhat,” often with an undesirable quality. It is not the “some” used before a noun; learners may put the adjective before 有些 or read the phrase as a quantity.

items.en: The room is somewhat old.
items.wrongPy: wū zi jiù yǒu xiē
items.why: 有些 must come before 旧, not after it; use the original order.

items.en: Actually, I’m somewhat worried.
items.wrongPy: qí shí wǒ zháo jí yǒu xiē
items.why: 有些 must come before 着急, not after it; use the original order.

items.note: Use 不 + adjective + 不 + contrasting adjective for a conventional description between two extremes. It does not work with every adjective pair; learners sometimes move the second 不 after its adjective.

items.en: The room is neither new nor old.
items.wrongPy: wū zi bù xīn jiù bù
items.why: The second 不 must precede 旧; the correct order is 屋子不新不旧。

items.en: The box is neither new nor old.
items.wrongPy: xiāng zi bù xīn jiù bù
items.why: The second 不 must precede 旧; the correct order is 箱子不新不旧。

items.note: Put 根据 before the basis, then state the conclusion or information supported by it. Learners may confuse the order of the basis and statement, or move a location phrase away from its noun.

items.en: According to the news, the world is changing.
items.wrongPy: gēn jù xīn wén biàn huà yǒu shì jiè
items.why: 有 must come before its object 世界; the correct statement is 世界有变化。

items.phrase: 根据名单客人都在屋子中
items.zh: 根据名单，客人都在屋子中。
items.en: According to the list, all the guests are inside the room.
items.wrong: 根据名单，客人都在中屋子。
items.wrongPy: gēn jù míng dān kè rén dōu zài zhōng wū zi
items.why: 中 follows 屋子 in this location phrase; the correct order is 客人都在屋子中。

items.note: Two adjacent noun phrases can identify the same person or thing, with the second clarifying the first. Keep the predicate after both expressions; learners may put part of the predicate before the identifying name.

items.en: The principal, Old Wang, is very healthy.
items.wrongPy: xiào zhǎng lǎo wáng jiàn kāng hěn
items.why: 很 must precede 健康; the correct sentence is 校长老王很健康。

items.en: My uncle, Wang, is very healthy.
items.wrongPy: wǒ shū shu lǎo wáng jiàn kāng hěn
items.why: 很 must precede 健康; the correct sentence is 我叔叔老王很健康。

items.note: 就 comes before the predicate or focused choice to emphasize insistence, immediacy, or a specific selection. Learners often put 就 after the verb or at the end of the phrase instead.

items.en: I'll just take this box.
items.wrongPy: wǒ xuǎn jiù zhè ge xiāng zi
items.why: 就 must precede the focused verb 选; the correct sentence is 我就选这个箱子。

items.en: I’ll choose this one and not that one.
items.wrongPy: wǒ xuǎn jiù zhè ge bù xuǎn nà ge
items.why: 就 must precede 选; the correct sentence is 我就选这个，不选那个。

items.note: 不一会儿 goes at the start to say that an event happens after a short interval. Use it before the event clause; learners often put 了 after the subject instead of after the event.

items.en: Soon, there was mail in the mailbox.
items.wrongPy: bù yí huìr yóu xiāng le yǒu xìn
items.why: 了 cannot go between the subject and 有; put it after the event, as in 邮箱有信了.

items.phrase: 不一会儿比赛有变化了
items.zh: 不一会儿，比赛有变化了。
items.en: Soon after, the competition changed.
items.wrong: 不一会儿，比赛了有变化。
items.wrongPy: bù yí huìr bǐ sài le yǒu biàn huà
items.why: 了 cannot go between 比赛 and 有; put it after the event, as in 比赛有变化了.

items.phrase: 不一会儿屋子有客人了
items.zh: 不一会儿，屋子有客人了。
items.en: Soon after, there were guests in the room.
items.wrong: 不一会儿，屋子了有客人。
items.wrongPy: bù yí huìr wū zi le yǒu kè rén
items.why: 了 cannot go between the subject and 有; put it after the event, as in 屋子有客人了.

items.note: Verb + 什么 + 啊 challenges or rejects an action; it is not a neutral question asking for an object. Keep 什么 after the verb and 啊 at the end, rather than reversing their order.

items.en: What are you getting anxious about!
items.wrongPy: zháo jí a shén me
items.why: 什么 must follow 着急 and 啊 should close the challenge, so keep 着急什么啊.

items.note: 在 + person + 看来 marks the following judgement as that person's viewpoint. Keep 看来 after the person; learners may wrongly treat 看来 as a verb that comes before its subject.

items.phrase: 在叔叔看来客人很热情
items.zh: 在叔叔看来，客人很热情。
items.en: In my uncle’s view, the guests are very warm and friendly.
items.wrong: 在看来叔叔，客人很热情。
items.wrongPy: zài kàn lái shū shu kè rén hěn rè qíng
items.why: 看来 must follow 叔叔 in this viewpoint pattern, so use 在叔叔看来.

items.phrase: 在叔叔看来羽毛球很容易
items.zh: 在叔叔看来，羽毛球很容易。
items.en: In my uncle’s view, badminton is easy.
items.wrong: 在看来叔叔，羽毛球很容易。
items.wrongPy: zài kàn lái shū shu yǔ máo qiú hěn róng yì
items.why: 看来 must follow 叔叔 in this viewpoint pattern, so use 在叔叔看来.

items.note: A time or event followed by 以前、以后、前 or 后 sets a before-or-after reference for the statement. 在 may come before that time or event, but learners should not insert particles inside the time phrase.

items.en: After the meeting, my uncle takes a vacation.
items.wrong: 在开会以后，叔叔了休假。
items.wrongPy: zài kāi huì yǐ hòu shū shu le xiū jià
items.why: 了 cannot go between 叔叔 and 休假; put it after the verb or omit it, as in 叔叔休假.

items.phrase: 在比赛以后他们去体育馆
items.zh: 在比赛以后，他们去体育馆。
items.en: After the competition, they go to the gym.
items.wrong: 在比赛以后，他们去在体育馆。
items.wrongPy: zài bǐ sài yǐ hòu tā men qù zài tǐ yù guǎn
items.why: 在 cannot follow 去 in this destination phrase; keep 去体育馆.

items.note: The pattern places 得很 after an adjective or adjective phrase to express a high degree, as in “very unpleasant.” Use it for intensity, not the manner of an action; learners often omit 得 or attach the pattern to a verb.

items.en: It sounds very unpleasant.
items.wrongPy: nán tīng hěn
items.why: The degree marker 得 must follow 难听; without it, 很 cannot form this adjective degree complement.

items.en: The sound is very clear.
items.wrongPy: shēng yīn qīng chu hěn
items.why: The degree marker 得 must follow 清楚; without it, 很 cannot form this adjective degree complement.

items.note: Here, the quality or state is the topic being evaluated, and 才行 or 不行 gives the judgment. Use this pattern to say whether a condition is acceptable; learners may misorder 才 or mistake the quality phrase for an action.

items.en: Being healthy is essential.
items.wrongPy: cái jiàn kāng xíng
items.why: 才 follows the quality before 行; placing it first breaks the required evaluation pattern.

items.note: 该 + verb phrase + 了 signals that it is time to act now. It is more specific than general advice; learners often put 了 immediately after 该 instead of at the end of the verb phrase.

items.en: It’s time to replace the air conditioner.
items.wrongPy: gāi le huàn kōng tiáo
items.why: 该 must precede the action, while 了 closes the time-to-act pattern; inserting it after 该 is wrong.

items.en: It’s time to practice badminton.
items.wrongPy: gāi le liàn xí yǔ máo qiú
items.why: 该 must precede the action, while 了 closes the time-to-act pattern; inserting it after 该 is wrong.

items.note: Place the possessive first, then the quantity phrase, then the descriptive modifier and noun. This order identifies one old suitcase belonging to the speaker; learners often move the adjective before the quantity phrase or confuse which modifier it describes.

items.phrase: 我的一个旧箱子在屋子中间
items.zh: 我的一个旧箱子在屋子中间。
items.en: One of my old suitcases is in the middle of the room.
items.wrong: 旧我的一个箱子在屋子中间。
items.wrongPy: jiù wǒ de yí gè xiāng zi zài wū zi zhōng jiān
items.why: 旧 must modify 箱子 after the quantity phrase, not precede 我的; the correct order is 我的一个旧箱子.

items.note: Put 出 immediately after a verb when it marks a result, such as discovering or producing something, rather than physical movement outward. The result object follows 出. Learners often put 出 after the object, confusing this result complement with a separate direction.

items.en: I found the number.
items.wrongPy: wǒ chá hào mǎ chū le yī
items.why: 出 must follow 查 and precede the object; the correct order is 我查出号码了。

items.note: 不是 + statement + 吗？ turns an affirmative fact into a rhetorical reminder, usually expecting agreement. Keep 不是 before the whole statement and 吗 at the end. Learners often move 不是 inside the predicate or treat the question as a neutral request for information.

items.en: You have an email address, don’t you?
items.wrongPy: nǐ yǒu bú shì yóu xiāng ma
items.why: 不是 must precede the whole statement, so the correct form is 你不是有邮箱吗？

items.en: Don’t you need takeout?
items.wrongPy: nǐ xū yào bú shì wài mài ma
items.why: 不是 must precede the whole statement, so the correct form is 你不是需要外卖吗？

items.note: Place 了 after the elapsed interval to say how much time has passed since a bounded event ended. This differs from measuring how long an action lasted. Learners often place 了 before the interval, which makes it sound like the event itself continued for that long.

items.en: It’s been a day since the move.
items.wrongPy: bān jiā le yì tiān
items.why: Here 了 before 一天 makes the interval sound like the duration of moving; for time since the move, say 搬家一天了。

items.note: In a 把 sentence, put the identifiable object after 把 and before the verb; the direction complement follows the verb. Learners often put the complement before the verb, even though it must complete the verb that describes the action.

items.en: I selected the photos.
items.wrongPy: wǒ bǎ zhào piàn chū lái xuǎn
items.why: 出来 must follow 选 as its complement, so the correct order is 我把照片选出来。

items.en: I put away the old photos.
items.wrongPy: wǒ bǎ jiù zhào piàn qǐ lai shōu
items.why: 起来 must follow 收 as its complement, so the correct order is 我把旧照片收起来。

items.note: Use 把 when the known object is acted on, then 得 after the verb to describe the object's resulting state. This emphasizes the outcome; learners often put 得 before the verb or omit it.

items.en: I explained the conversation very clearly.
items.wrongPy: wǒ bǎ duì huà de jiǎng hěn qīng chu
items.why: 得 follows the verb and precedes the state complement; the correct order is 讲得很清楚.

items.en: I took the photo very clearly.
items.wrongPy: wǒ bǎ zhào piàn de zhào hěn qīng chu
items.why: 得 follows the verb and precedes the state complement; the correct order is 照得很清楚.

items.note: Use 把 plus a known object, a transfer verb, and 给 plus the recipient. In these examples, 给 introduces who receives the item; learners often put the recipient before 给.

items.en: I lent him the e-book.
items.wrongPy: wǒ bǎ diàn zǐ shū jiè tā gěi
items.why: 给 must come before the recipient, so the correct phrase is 借给他.

items.phrase: 她把电子书借给叔叔了
items.zh: 她把电子书借给叔叔了。
items.en: She lent the e-book to her uncle.
items.wrong: 她把电子书借叔叔了给。
items.wrongPy: tā bǎ diàn zǐ shū jiè shū shu le gěi
items.why: 给 must come before the recipient, so the correct phrase is 借给叔叔了.

items.note: Put 比 and the reference before 多 or 少, then the verb and quantity phrase; this compares how much an action occurs. Learners often move 多 or 少 before the reference.

items.en: He practices much more than I do.
items.wrongPy: tā bǐ duō wǒ liàn xí hěn duō
items.why: 多 comes after the reference 我, not before it; the correct order is 比我多练习.

items.phrase: 叔叔比阿姨多练习一会儿
items.zh: 叔叔比阿姨多练习一会儿。
items.en: Uncle practices a little longer than Aunt.
items.wrong: 叔叔比多阿姨练习一会儿。
items.wrongPy: shū shu bǐ duō ā yí liàn xí yí huìr
items.why: 多 comes after the reference 阿姨, not before it; the correct order is 比阿姨多练习.

items.note: Place 早 or 晚 after 比 plus the reference, followed by the action and duration. Use this to state how much earlier or later an action occurs; learners often put the time word before the reference.

items.phrase: 阿姨比叔叔早一会儿回家
items.zh: 阿姨比叔叔早一会儿回家。
items.en: Auntie gets home a little earlier than Uncle.
items.wrong: 阿姨比早叔叔一会儿回家。
items.wrongPy: ā yí bǐ zǎo shū shu yí huìr huí jiā
items.why: 早 follows the reference 叔叔, not 比; the correct order is 比叔叔早一会儿回家.

items.note: Use 不比 before the reference and adjective to deny that the subject exceeds it; this does not prove the subject is less. Learners often mistake it for a definite “less than” comparison.

items.phrase: 这个屋子不比那个屋子旧
items.zh: 这个屋子不比那个屋子旧。
items.en: This room is no older than that room.
items.wrong: 这个屋子不比旧那个屋子。
items.wrongPy: zhè ge wū zi bù bǐ jiù nà ge wū zi
items.why: 旧 must follow both compared nouns as the final adjective; the correct order is 这个屋子不比那个屋子旧.

items.note: Use 跟……一样…… to say two things share an equal degree of a quality. Keep 一样 before the adjective; learners often put it after the adjective or confuse this pattern with merely saying two things resemble one another.

items.en: Uncle is just as worried as Auntie.
items.wrongPy: shū shu gēn yí yàng ā yí zháo jí
items.why: 一样 must follow the reference item and come before the adjective; say 叔叔跟阿姨一样着急.

items.phrase: 这个季节跟那个季节一样长
items.zh: 这个季节跟那个季节一样长。
items.en: This season is as long as that season.
items.wrong: 这个季节跟一样那个季节长。
items.wrongPy: zhè ge jì jié gēn yí yàng nà ge jì jié cháng
items.why: 一样 must come after the reference item, not before it; say 这个季节跟那个季节一样长.

items.note: Use 或者 before each of two alternative clauses when presenting alternatives. Learners often place 或者 after an option instead of introducing it.

items.en: Either practice or exercise.
items.wrongPy: liàn xí huò zhě huò zhě duàn liàn
items.why: 或者 must introduce each option, not follow the first one; say 或者练习，或者锻炼.

items.note: Use a location followed by an appearance verb, its result or direction complement, 了, then a quantity and entity. Learners often put 了 after the quantity instead of before it.

items.phrase: 体育馆里来了很多客人
items.zh: 体育馆里来了很多客人。
items.en: A lot of guests came to the gym.
items.wrong: 里体育馆来了很多客人。
items.wrongPy: lǐ tǐ yù guǎn lái le hěn duō kè rén
items.why: 里 must follow the place noun, so the correct order is 体育馆里.

items.note: Use a location followed by a disappearance verb, its result complement, 了, then a quantity and entity. Learners may put 了 between the verb and complement, breaking their order.

items.phrase: 屋子里搬走了很多箱子
items.zh: 屋子里搬走了很多箱子。
items.en: A lot of boxes were moved out of the room.
items.wrong: 屋子里搬了走很多箱子。
items.wrongPy: wū zi lǐ bān le zǒu hěn duō xiāng zi
items.why: The result complement 走 must follow 搬 directly, so 了 belongs after 走.

items.phrase: 屋子里搬走了两个箱子
items.zh: 屋子里搬走了两个箱子。
items.en: Two boxes were moved out of the room.
items.wrong: 屋子里搬了走两个箱子。
items.wrongPy: wū zi lǐ bān le zǒu liǎng gè xiāng zi
items.why: The result complement 走 must follow 搬 directly, so 了 belongs after 走.

items.note: When a verb takes an object and a 得 complement, repeat the verb after the object so each part has its place. Learners often put 得 after the first verb, before its object.

items.en: He can see the photos clearly.
items.wrongPy: tā kàn de zhào piàn kàn hěn qīng chu
items.why: 得 cannot come between 看 and its object 照片; it follows the repeated verb.

items.en: He takes very clear photos.
items.wrongPy: tā zhào de zhào piàn zhào hěn qīng chu
items.why: 得 cannot come between 照 and its object 照片; it follows the repeated verb.

items.note: 大概 before a number and measure word gives an approximate quantity, not uncertainty about the whole statement. Use it with a noun to estimate how many or how much. Learners often mistake it for a sentence-level word meaning “probably.”

Put two adjacent numbers in ascending order before the measure word to give an approximate range, as in “three or four.” This is a conventional pattern, not a way to join any numbers. Learners may reverse the numbers or mistake 都’s position.

items.en: Three or four guests are here.
items.wrongPy: sì sān gè kè rén dōu zài
items.why: The adjacent-number range goes from lower to higher, so 三四个客人 is correct.

items.note: Use a completed first action followed by 了就 and the next action to express “once X happens, then Y.” 就 may be omitted, and 了 does not necessarily mean past time. Learners often put 了 after 就 instead of after the first action.

items.en: Once you get used to it, keep going.
items.wrongPy: xí guàn le jiù le jiān chí
items.why: 了 cannot go between 就 and the next action; 习惯了就坚持 is correct.

items.en: Turn it on, then practice.
items.wrongPy: kāi jī le jiù le liàn xí
items.why: 了 cannot go between 就 and the next action; 开机了就练习 is correct.

items.note: Use 又 before each of two compatible actions to say that both occur; they need not happen simultaneously. The actions can be activities or other compatible events. Learners often put the second 又 after its action instead of before it.

items.en: Practice and exercise, too.
items.wrongPy: yòu liàn xí duàn liàn yòu
items.why: 又 must precede each action; 又练习又锻炼 is the correct pattern.

items.en: The guests both chat and take photos.
items.wrongPy: kè rén yòu liáo tiānr pāi zhào yòu
items.why: 又 must precede 拍照; 客人又聊天儿又拍照 is the correct order.

items.note: Use 越来越 before a gradable quality or attitude to show that its degree is changing over time. It does not freely combine with arbitrary actions; learners often put the quality before 越来越 instead of after it.

items.en: He understands language better and better.
items.wrongPy: tā yuè lái yuè yǔ yán liǎo jiě
items.why: 了解 must precede its object; say 他越来越了解语言, not 他越来越语言了解.

items.en: She likes badminton more and more.
items.wrongPy: tā yuè lái yuè yǔ máo qiú xǐ ài
items.why: 喜爱 must precede its object; say 她越来越喜爱羽毛球, not 她越来越羽毛球喜爱.

items.note: Put a sound-producing verb before a number-plus-classifier phrase with 声 to count a discrete vocalization, such as a shout or call. Learners often put the number and classifier after the sound noun; they belong before it.

items.en: A team member gave a shout.
items.wrongPy: duì yuán fā chū hǎn yì shēng
items.why: The number-classifier phrase must come before the sound noun; the original puts 一声 before 喊.

items.note: Put 是 before an evaluated predicate and 的 after it to give an emphatic opinion or assurance. Learners may mistake this for the 是……的 pattern that focuses on circumstances of a past event.

items.en: He left the work behind.
items.wrongPy: zuò pǐn shì liú de tā
items.why: The object 他 cannot follow 的 here; the correct order is 作品是他留的.

items.en: This chart is standard.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge biǎo shì de biāo zhǔn
items.why: 的 must follow the evaluated predicate, so the correct ending is 标准的.

items.phrase: 这个方法是比较简单的
items.zh: 这个方法是比较简单的。
items.en: This method is relatively simple.
items.wrong: 这个方法是简单比较的。
items.wrongPy: zhè ge fāng fǎ shì jiǎn dān bǐ jiào de
items.why: 比较 modifies 简单 and must come before it, so the correct order is 比较简单.

items.note: Put 着 after the accompanying action or posture and before the main action; the subject is shared. Learners often attach 着 to the object or put it after the main verb instead.

items.en: He is holding a box.
items.wrongPy: tā zhe bào hé zi
items.why: 着 follows the accompanying verb 抱, not the subject; say 他抱着盒子.

items.en: I’m keeping the work.
items.wrongPy: zuò pǐn zhe wǒ liú zhe
items.why: In this topic-comment sentence, 着 follows 留, not 作品; say 作品我留着.

items.en: I’m hurrying to check the score.
items.wrongPy: wǒ gǎn chá kàn zhe fēn shù
items.why: 着 follows 赶 to mark the accompanying action; say 我赶着查看分数.

items.en: They chat while watching the news.
items.wrongPy: kàn xīn wén zhe liáo tiānr
items.why: 着 follows 看 and comes before its object 新闻; say 看着新闻聊天儿.

items.en: The bucket is upside down, and the box is too.
items.wrongPy: tǒng dào zhe hé zi zhe yě dào zhe
items.why: 也 comes before the predicate, while 着 follows 倒; say 桶倒着，盒子也倒着.
